title: Scheduler mode enforcement after B1 confirmation

root_cause.rule: refused a Track 1 shadow start because the confirmation FILE EXISTS
root_cause.stated_reason: that file arms the Track 1 route
root_cause.why_it_expired: true when the signature was the only thing between this route and an order; Stage 5S added a measured evidence gate and Stage 5ZZK gave B1 a measured half, so the file no longer arms anything by itself
sequence: operator signs the B1 decision -> confirmation file exists
--track1-only-shadow now REFUSES because of that file
scheduler restarted without any Track 1 flag -> 45 legacy entry jobs registered on the very login the signature had just declared retired
root_cause.one_line: the guard pushed the operator out of the only safe mode and into the unsafe one
root_cause.not_a_missing_check: a check whose premise had expired, with nothing failing loudly when it did

part_a_before.verified_not_assumed: an earlier probe printed the command line one character per line, which would have meant the mode detection was type-confused and the alarm a false positive; scheduler_command_lines returns a single string, the substring test is correct, and the argv above is real

second_defect_found.truth: a statement about a process that had ALREADY EXITED - last [track1-only] registration line 2026-08-27 05:08:33, running scheduler started 21:51:23 and registered none
second_defect_found.principle: a freshness check that compares the code against a dead process's log reports on the wrong system with full confidence

part_b_implementation.chosen: Option A - relax the guard, do not invent a mode
part_b_implementation.why: there is nothing wrong with --track1-only-shadow: it already registers no legacy entry job, keeps legacy's safety sweeps draining the old book, and cannot send an order. A new mode name would have been a second thing to explain and a second thing to keep in step.
part_b_implementation.new_rule: the confirmation file blocks a shadow start only when the GATE REGISTRY reports every order blocker clear
part_b_implementation.why_the_registry: since 5ZZK it reads the confirmation file AND the measurement behind every blocker - it is the thing that knows
part_b_implementation.half_of_the_old_guard_kept: if every blocker really is clear, a shadow start is starting something nobody asked for
part_b_implementation.fails_closed: orders_would_be_possible reports 'possible' when the registry cannot be read, so a guard built on it refuses rather than waving a start through on a question it could not answer

part_c_missing_guard.what_it_refuses: a scheduler start that would register legacy ENTRY jobs while a signed B1 decision says legacy has retired from this login
part_c_missing_guard.why_it_was_missing: track1_shadow_blockers always asked whether a TRACK 1 start was safe; nothing asked whether a LEGACY start was, and the answer stopped being 'always' the moment an operator signed
names_four_things: this start would register 45 legacy entry jobs on that same login
if legacy must run entries again, retire the decision first
part_c_missing_guard.placement: before EITHER launch path, next to the existing flags-conflict refusal
part_c_missing_guard.why_that_placement: restart --scheduler stops the running process first; a guard that fired after that would leave the operator with no scheduler at all
part_c_missing_guard.proven: with the guard tripped, ensure_single, stop_runners and start_scheduler are all untouched and the command returns 2
part_c_missing_guard.why_not: it adds Track 1's slots and keeps all 45 legacy entry jobs - exactly the collision B1 exists to prevent
part_c_missing_guard.one_table_three_readers: both guards count from legacy_retirement_candidates, the same table the scheduler's removal step and the retirement audit read, so the number in the refusal cannot drift from the number registered

part_d_status.conflict_line: MODE CONFLICT - the B1 decision says legacy is retired for this login, and the running scheduler registers 45 legacy entry job(s) on it
part_d_status.why_three: a mode nobody could read is NOT a compatible mode, and printing it as one would be the fail-open this route keeps finding

stale_sentences_repaired.now: track1_slot_table=stale_log when the registration line predates the running process

stale_sentences_repaired.was: orders : impossible - B1 open and no confirmation file
stale_sentences_repaired.problem: false on BOTH halves after the operator signed, and went on printing
stale_sentences_repaired.now: orders : impossible - blocked by PAPER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE, asked of the registry

part_e_restart_command.how_verified: track1_shadow_blockers(track1_only=True) returns [] against the REAL signed confirmation, and the legacy guard exempts this mode by design
after_it: the 5ZZJ alarm passes BECAUSE the mode is compatible, not because anything was loosened
part_e_restart_command.orders_stay_impossible: PAPER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE is measured, not signed, and the approval variable is unset

part_f_backend.reason: /api/v1/track1-market-view was added in Stage 5ZZL and the running backend does not have it
part_f_backend.does_not_touch_scheduler: --no-scheduler leaves a running scheduler alone and prints its age; it does not start one and does not change its mode

tests.5zzj_alarm_pinned_as_strict: a test reads that file and asserts `capability != dec.LEGACY_ENTRY_PRESENT` is still present and has not become a skip
my_own_mistakes_caught_by_running: compared scheduler JOB ids against SLOT-TABLE ids - jobs register lowercase (track1_calm_decide_0932), the table names them TRACK1_CALM_DECIDE_0932
a test Namespace was missing api_port, so it ran past the guard into backend startup

slot_table_freshness scanned the LIVE process table inside itself, so two 5ZZ unit tests handing it a fixture log failed because the real scheduler outside started after their fixture's timestamp - a function that reads ambient state cannot be asked a hypothetical; the process start is now passed in
tests.failure_classification: the 5ZZJ alarm, still red because the running scheduler has not been restarted - the enforcement is in the code, not yet in the process; it clears with the Part E command

tests_isolated_not_weakened.why: they describe a LEGACY start and were reading the real machine's confirmation file, so they began failing for a reason that has nothing to do with process management
tests_isolated_not_weakened.how: pointed at a path that does not exist - the pre-B1 world they were written for

safety.external: scheduler pid 11332, started 2026-08-27 21:51:23 with no Track 1 flag - the restart that caused this, done outside these stages
